To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the side chains of amphipath helices of apoliproteins can be oriented in the lipid bilayer of lipoprotein discs in two different ways, depending on the size of the disc.
a synthetic amphipathic peptide of the apoprotein class interacts with the phospholipids of discoidal complexes to form an alpha-helical conformation.

the 13C-NMR spectra of [1-(13)CH(3)]Ala11-18A in discoid complexes with DMPC and in SUVs of egg PC show the 13CH(3) group to be in different environments in these two systems, consistent with the 13CH group being on the surface of the discoid complex and buried in the bilayer of the SUV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular interactions of the amphipathy of an apolipoprotein-like peptide with the phospholipids of the lipoproteins.
the structure of amphipathicity of the apolipo proteins in serum lipoprotein.
the structure of amphipathicity in apolipoprotein and how the structure is related to the location of apolipoprotein helices in lipoprotein disks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 13C-NMR spectra of 18A and 13C-Ala18A in the presence of DMPC and PC are consistent with the following: (1) The amphipathic nature of 18A results in its binding to the edge of the discoidal DMPC complex.
18A forms a helix in the aqueous environment and is amphipathic in nature.

the 13C-NMR spectra of 13CH3-labeled 18A-PC disks are consistent with 18A molecules being located on both the edge and the faces of the disk and that the 13CNMR spectra of the 13C-labled 18A-egg PC vesicles are consistent with 19A being located on the surface of the vesicle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
18A molecules in DMPC disks are oriented with the positive side of their amphipathic structure in contact with DM PC and the negative side in contact with water.
the amphipathicity of the apolipo protein class of peptides can be used to pack them in discoidal complexes and in small unilameller vesicles.
amphipathic peptides can be located on the edge and on the faces of discoidal complexes and that these locations are sensitive to the size of the complex and to the lipid packing in the disk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the apolar side chains of the 18-residue amphipathic peptide are located in the edge of the lipid disk.
amphipathic peptides can be used to probe the molecular packing of lipids and that the packing of the lipid bilayers is sensitive to the presence of amphipathics.
13CH3-labeled amino acids can be used to probe the location and motion of amphipathically helical peptides in discoidal complexes.
